title: Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Slack

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to specific Slack workspaces. With this functionality, you can enable selective monitoring of specific workspaces within your Slack enterprise account for DLP and Malware scanning.

When you create a custom connector for Slack for DLP and Malware scanning, you must provide the Slack workspace ID, client ID, client secret during tenant onboarding in the Zscaler Admin Console so that the Zscaler service can access the application. You must also configure the right permissions so that Zscaler can securely authorize the application.
To create a custom connector for Slack:

blocks.item: Log in to Slack API: Applications.
The Create New App window appears.
In the Create New App window, select Blank App and click Continue to create a custom connector from scratch.
In the Name app & choose workspace window, enter the following details:
App Name: Name of the app.
Workspace: Select a workspace from the available workspaces.
Click Create App to create the connector.
You're redirected to the OAuth & Permissions page under Settings.
On the OAuth & Permissions page under Redirect URLs, click Add New Redirect URL and enter the URL for your Zscaler server.
Under Scopes, enter the following bot and user scopes:
Under Bot Token Scopes, click Add an Oauth Scope and add the following Bot Scopes:
Under User Token Scopes, click Add an Oauth Scope and add the following User Scopes:
The discovery:read and discovery:write scopes are request-only scopes. You need to request the Slack team for approval of discovery scopes:
Raise a support request with the Slack team as described in this Slack documentation.
When approved, these scopes become available in the drop-down list.
Go to Manage Distribution under Settings and click Activate Distribution to allow installation.

blocks.text: While onboarding your Slack tenant, you're required to enter your Slack workspace ID. This ID depends on your Slack account type, for example, Enterprise Grid or Non-Grid (Enterprise Select, Pro, or Business+).
To find your Slack Workspace ID for your account type, follow the respective steps:

blocks.item: Log in to your Slack organization.
Click the organization name in the left-side navigation.
Go to Organization Settings under Tools & Settings.
Go to All Workspaces under Workspaces.
Click the three-dot menu icon next to the workspace you want to scan.
Paste this Workspace ID into the Slack Workspace ID field on the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Log in to your Slack workspace.
The address bar shows the URL https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXX/CXXXXXXX
Copy the T-prefixed ID from the URL (the segment after /client/).
Paste this Workspace ID into the Slack Workspace ID field on the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
